candidates.name: 5-(6-hydroxybenzofuran-2-yl)-2,4-dimethoxybenzaldehyde
candidates.rationale: 10.02/187.8 is a CHO on a 2,4-dimethoxy ring (cf. 2,4-dimethoxybenzaldehyde, CHO 188.3, C-1 near 119.3). On that ring H-6 is 8.01 (s), H-3 is 6.71 and C-3 is 96.6. A 2-aryl-6-hydroxybenzofuran accounts for H-4 7.52, H-3 7.18, H-7 7.00 and H-5 6.66, with C-7 at 100.6 and C-7a at 156.3. The O-bearing carbons are 163.6, 162.6, 160.1, 159.8 and 156.3. The 15 non-OMe carbons give 15 signals, and the OH is unlisted.

candidates.name: 4-hydroxy-2-methoxy-5-(6-methoxybenzofuran-2-yl)benzaldehyde
candidates.rationale: Same 2-arylbenzofuran aldehyde skeleton as rank 1, with the OH and one OMe swapped between the two rings. It fits the CHO (1, 10), the two OMe (8, 9, 25) and the same six aromatic CH (2-7) equally well on the 1D data.

candidates.name: 4-(6-hydroxy-4-methoxybenzofuran-2-yl)-2-methoxybenzaldehyde
candidates.rationale: Alternative placement: a 4-formyl-3-methoxyphenyl ring (H 8.01, 7.52) carries a 6-hydroxy-4-methoxybenzofuran (H-3 7.18, H-7 6.71, H-5 6.66). It is less favoured because C-7 of such a ring is expected near 89 ppm, which is absent.

first.reasoning_summary: DoU is 11. The 13C at 187.8 with 1H 10.02 indicates a conjugated aryl aldehyde with an ortho-OMe, rather than a flavone or aurone carbonyl. There are two OMe groups (3.88 and 3.86, 3H each) on a shared 13C at 56.2, so 16 signals cover all 17 C. Six aromatic CH (6.66-8.01) + CHO + 2 OMe = 13 H; the 14th H is an unlisted phenolic OH. Five oxygenated sp2 carbons (156-164) fit benzofuran C-2 and C-7a plus two C-OMe and one C-OH. A 2-arylbenzofuran carbaldehyde (C14H10O core, DoU 10, +CHO = 11) carrying OH + 2 OMe matches C17H14O5. Shifts at 119.3 (C-1 of the aldehyde ring), 96.6 and 100.6 (CH between or near oxygens) and 133.7 (CH ortho to CHO) best fit a 2,4-dimethoxybenzaldehyde ring bearing a 6-hydroxybenzofuran-2-yl at C-5. The OH/OMe placements cannot be fixed without 2D data.

evidence.note: 187.8 is a conjugated aryl ketone (the aurone C-3 carbonyl); it is outside the aldehyde range.
10.02 is a phenolic OH in acetone-d6, on C-6 near 163.6.
Two OCH3 singlets at 3.88 and 3.86 share one 13C at 56.2.
Aryl methyl ethers plus the furanone ring oxygen.
The methyls are the OCH3 groups.

candidates.name: 6-hydroxy-3',4'-dimethoxyaurone (sulfuretin 3',4'-dimethyl ether)
candidates.rationale: Aurone skeleton (DoU 11) with the ketone at 187.8 (10). The phenolic OH is 10.02 (1) and the two OMe are 8, 9 and 25. The 7 CH appear as 6 signals (2-7), so one signal holds 2H. The O-bearing carbons are 11-15, and the exocyclic CH is near 109.9. The H count is 14.

candidates.name: 7-hydroxy-3',4'-dimethoxyflavone
candidates.rationale: Flavone isomer with the same substituents. The carbonyl at 187.8 (10) is high for a flavone C-4. Assignments otherwise mirror rank 1 (1-9).

candidates.name: 4'-hydroxy-6,3'-dimethoxyaurone
candidates.rationale: Aurone with the OH and OMe groups placed differently; it fits peaks 1-10 and 25 similarly.

repaired.reasoning_summary: The 187.8 carbon lies outside the aldehyde range, so it is a conjugated ketone. 10.02 is then a phenolic OH in acetone-d6. 1H count: OH (1) + 7 aromatic/vinyl CH in 6 signals (2-7) + 2 OMe (8, 9) = 14, which matches C17H14O5. DoU 11 fits an aurone or flavone core carrying one OH and two OMe. An aurone is favoured because a ketone near 188 is high for a flavone C-4. The OH/OMe positions are tentative without coupling data.
